messages:
alex (Sales): Quick one — ACME POC asked for strict EU-only processing for inference and logs. They want: 1) model runtime & KV cache never leave EU, 2) list of sub-processors in region, 3) routing guarantee to EU endpoints (no accidental fallbacks to us-east). Also asking whether region pinning adds cost for Dedicated vs Hosted.

acme-poc (Customer): Can you confirm whether IPs or peering are required? They prefer not to open wide egress.

maya (Solutions): short answer: yes we can do EU-only for Hosted via regional endpoints + routing policy. For Dedicated/Private it's easier — you control the network. Need to clarify whether they want geo-fence at the control plane level or strict network egress blocking.

jordan (SRE): For Hosted: we have region-aware routing and an additional tenant-level flag `region_preference`. It prefers EU endpoints and only falls back to other regions if capacity is exhausted. We can disable cross-region fallback for enterprise accounts. No automatic data egress for KV cache if region lock enabled.

maya (Solutions): POC steps I recommend: 1) enable `region_preference: eu` on tenant, 2) set `cross_region_fallback: false` for the trial, 3) use our EU streaming endpoint `https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` for requests.

alex (Sales): cost question from customer: does locking routing to EU change per-token pricing or is there an add-on?

maya (Solutions): Routing/region preference itself is a free config on Hosted for Enterprise tier, but reserved Dedicated capacity may change unit economics (you pay for capacity commit). If they want guaranteed capacity in eu-west-1, that's a Dedicated/reserved contract.

acme-poc (Customer): If we pick Hosted + region lock, are there any subprocessors outside EU that could see metadata? They need subprocessor list + SOC/SCCs.

sophie (Legal): We'll share the current subprocessor list filtered by region. For Hosted EU-only with region_lock enabled, primary subprocessors for compute/storage are EU-based cloud infra partners (list to be attached), and we provide SCCs + Data Processing Addendum. If they require all subprocessors to be EU, we may need Dedicated in a customer-selected cloud region or Private.

jordan (SRE): Operational details: to completely avoid cross-region peering, set `cross_region_fallback: false` and we'll set a hard route policy on the tenant. Note: if capacity spikes beyond reserved capacity and fallback is disabled, requests will receive 429s rather than routing out of region. We'll also provide a list of egress IP ranges for EU endpoints for firewall/peering.

maya (Solutions): here's a sample config snippet they can apply during the POC:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-123",
  "region_preference": "eu",
  "cross_region_fallback": false,
  "ingress_endpoint": "https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1",
  "allow_model_variant_fallback": false
}
```

alex (Sales): Perfect. Can someone craft a short one-pager for ACME listing: sub-processors (EU), routing guarantees, what breaks if fallback disabled, and pricing impact for Dedicated vs Hosted? Need it by EOD for the Exec.

sophie (Legal): I'll draft the subprocessor + DPA snippet.

jordan (SRE): I'll add the IP ranges + operational notes (429 behavior, metrics to monitor).

maya (Solutions): I'll cover the config steps and POC checklist (test traffic, edge-case: long KV cache reuse across tenants — confirm it's never replicated cross-region).

deploy-bot: Deployment note: region_lock feature is enabled on staging for account acme-123 (build 2026.3.18-74). Please validate. :white_check_mark:

acme-poc (Customer): thanks — we'll run a short traffic test tomorrow and share results.

alex (Sales): thanks team — looping in account exec for follow-up. :thumbsup:
